text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It’s the fastest way to catch routing errors and quality issues in completed work before they compound. The trade-off is delayed feedback on open PRs, but merged PRs represent the highest risk of undetected flaws slipping into production.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs is too late—it catches errors *after* they’re already in production, not before. A better alternative is running PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first, where fixes prevent compounding flaws. Settle it by measuring the delta in post-merge incidents between the two approaches over a month.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first, then expand to merged PRs—this catches flaws earlier while still validating the approach on completed work. The trade-off is higher initial effort, but it reduces post-merge incidents by catching issues before they compound.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first. It catches routing flaws and quality issues before they compound, reducing post-merge incidents. The trade-off is delayed validation on merged PRs, but open PRs represent the highest risk of undetected flaws slipping into production.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first, then expand to merged PRs—this catches flaws earlier while reducing post-merge incidents. The result must be a live shadow-mode run on the newest open PR with incident metrics tracked for 30 days. Overhaul owns delivery.
